## Work log

<!-- Chronological, written as you go. What was actually done, why, what it cost.
     Reference commits and link to plans and notes. Prose beats a checklist here —
     this is the part you will actually reread in three months. -->

- The ask was "a hidden route where internal users can generate STL files of the Wat Ket
  3D map". The first real decision was what *hidden* can mean here, and the answer is
  narrower than it sounds: `output: 'export'` means there is no server, so there is no
  auth to put in front of anything. The options were an unlinked-but-published page, a
  client-side passphrase (a doormat, not a lock — the check ships in the bundle), or
  absence. Chose absence: `src/app/print/` is in `.vercelignore`, the Vercel build never
  receives the directory, and a build with it moved aside produces exactly the two routes
  it did before. Local dev and a local `npm run build` still have it, which is the
  exhibition laptop — the machine that will actually drive a printer.

- Then the second ask: tile it for a Bambu A1 mini. This is the constraint that decides
  the design rather than decorating it. The near geometry is 2,500 m across and the bed is
  180 mm, so there is no scale at which one plate holds Wat Ket. Tiles interlock with tabs
  cut into the plate outline — a 2D polygon operation before extrusion — rather than pegs
  and sockets, because a socket is a hole, a hole is a boolean, and a boolean is a CSG
  library this project does not have.

- The default: 2,500 m at 1:7,143 as 2 × 2 plates of 175 mm, 179 mm on the bed with their
  tabs, 46 mm tall, 154,316 triangles, 15.4 MB of STL. Heights exaggerated three times,
  which is not a flourish — the median Wat Ket building is 5.08 m and prints at 0.71 mm
  honestly, under two layer lines. The factor is on screen, in each STL's 80-byte header
  and in the README inside the download, for the same reason the valley view puts its
  four-times in the caption.

- **The bug worth remembering.** The first version extruded through `merge.ts`'s
  `buildingGeometry`, to keep the print and the screen literally sharing one call. A
  manifold check over the real scene found eight unmatched edges per layer — small, but
  exactly what makes a slicer say "needs repair". One building in 7,588 causes it:
  `osm/way/822116040` is concave and straddles a tile seam, `clipRingToConvex` cuts it into
  two pieces joined by a zero-width neck (which `clip.ts` warns about in its own docstring),
  earcut correctly drops the neck from the caps, and `ExtrudeGeometry` then raises walls
  along a ring the caps no longer follow. Fixed by raising walls on the cap triangulation's
  own boundary edges, which cannot disagree with it whatever the ring did. Every layer of
  every tile is closed now, and the test file checks edge pairing on a U-shape straddling a
  seam. What is still shared with the viewer is `footprintToExtrudeArgs` and the same earcut
  call — the part that actually decides what a footprint means.

- **The hour I would like back.** The form silently refused to submit. No console error, no
  visible bubble, the button never even repainted to "Building…". HTML5 `step` validation is
  `(value - min) % step` evaluated in binary floating point, so a 2 mm plate against
  `min=0.6 step=0.2` is a "step mismatch" — (2 − 0.6) / 0.2 is 7.000000000000001 — and the
  browser blocks submission. The form is `noValidate` now and states its own constraints.

- Verified end to end rather than by eye: 475 tests green, a headless build of the real scene
  reporting zero unmatched edges on every layer of every tile, `unzip -t` clean on the 25-file
  archive, and each STL re-read with an independent Python parser — r1c1 measures 0–179 mm in
  X against its 175 mm plate (the 4 mm east tab) and r2c2 0–179 in Y (its north tab), both
  inside the 180 mm bed. In the browser: the plan draws, Enter on Build builds, focus lands on
  the stats, Escape clears.

### Print one tile before trusting any of this

<details>
<summary>Everything is verified except the only thing that matters</summary>

The geometry is checked, the container is checked, the dimensions are checked against the
A1 mini's bed. What is not checked is a printed object: whether a 0.6 mm raised road reads
at 1:7,143 through a 0.4 mm nozzle, and whether 0.2 mm of tab clearance is enough in PLA at
this size. Both are in the plan's open questions. Neither is answerable at a desk.

Slice `wat-ket_r1c1_combined.stl` with an A1 mini profile first — it is the tile with the
river through it and the most going on.
</details>

## Notes

<!-- Decisions made, things learned, blockers, what carries into tomorrow.
     Anything that changes the project's direction belongs in CLAUDE.md or the architecture
     docs as well — the diary is the trail, not the source of truth. -->

- **`.vercelignore` is a real gate and an env flag is not**, on a static export. Recorded in
  CLAUDE.md under Stack. The line that excludes `src/app/print/` is load-bearing: deleting it
  publishes the tool, and nothing in the code would stop it.

- **A 3D print is an ODbL Produced Work** and leaves the repo with no footer attached to it.
  `printSummary` writes the sources into the `README.txt` inside every download. Noted in the
  README's licensing section beside the viewer-footer rule, because the failure mode is the
  same one: add a source, forget the credit.

- Carrying forward: nothing blocking. The print tool does not touch the scene schema, `terrain`
  is still `null`, and none of this is on the 24 Sep critical path — it is an object for the
  room, not part of the piece.
